items.stem: A test is 99% accurate for a rare disease. A positive result alone does NOT strongly imply disease mainly because:

options.text: With a rare condition, false positives can outnumber true positives
options.rationale: Correct: base rates make positives mostly false when the condition is rare.

options.text: 99% accuracy means the test is useless
options.rationale: The test is useful but base rate still matters.

options.text: Probability does not apply to medicine

options.rationale: They are linked through base rates.

items.explanation: Correct: base rates make positives mostly false when the condition is rare.

items.stem: What does the expected value of a random variable represent?

options.text: The long-run average outcome over many repetitions
options.rationale: Correct: it is the probability-weighted mean.

options.text: The single outcome that will definitely occur
options.rationale: It is not a guaranteed single outcome.
It is an average, not a maximum.
Variance measures spread, not the mean.
